# Suspect event classification
Note: The concept of a "suspect" event flag was considered during method development — specifically, flagging peak flow events where total antecedent WLDAS modeled forcing was insufficient to reliably characterize the generating process. Two empirical tests were conducted to evaluate whether such a flag was operationalizable: (1) examination of the marginal distribution of total antecedent forcing depth across all POT peaks, and (2) examination of the forcing-response relationship (total antecedent forcing depth vs. observed peak flow expressed as mm/day over basin area). Neither test revealed a natural break or distinct outlier population that would justify a data-driven threshold. The forcing distribution is unimodal and approximately log-normal with no low-forcing cluster, and high runoff ratio events are scattered continuously across the full range of forcing depths rather than concentrated at low forcing values. On this basis, the suspect flag was rejected as an unsupportable imposition of structure not present in the data.

WLDAS coverage is complete across the study period with no incomplete accumulation windows, so no data availability-based exclusions are required either.

For the adaptive pipeline, this means all valid POT peaks receive a rain_frac value and are therefore classifiable — the unclassified category does not exist in the adaptive framework by design. For the fixed (Davenport) pipeline, an unclassified category is retained for events that do not exceed any per-process depth threshold, which is inherent to that classification scheme and consistent with Yu et al. (2022).

```{r suspect-event-classification-1}
library(tidyverse)

# --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
proj_root  <- "/Users/mtalbot/Desktop/GitHub/CoWC_FY26_Enhanced_Impacts/"
data_dir   <- file.path(proj_root, "_data")
diag_dir   <- file.path(proj_root, "_diagnostics", "threshold_evaluation")
dir.create(diag_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# --- Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
adaptive <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "pot_peaks_classified_adaptive.rds"))
meta     <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "site_metadata.rds"))

# Deduplicate to one row per peak
adaptive <- adaptive %>%
  distinct(site_no, peak_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Filter to unregulated sites
unreg_sites <- meta %>% filter(!regulated) %>% pull(site_no)
peaks_unreg <- adaptive %>% filter(site_no %in% unreg_sites)

# --- Partition by data availability -----------------------------------------
n_total      <- nrow(peaks_unreg)
n_incomplete <- sum(is.na(peaks_unreg$total_flux_short))
n_flux_valid <- n_total - n_incomplete

peaks_flux <- peaks_unreg %>%
  filter(!is.na(total_flux_short))

cat(sprintf(
  "Unregulated peaks: %d total | %d with valid flux | %d incomplete window (excluded)\n",
  n_total, n_flux_valid, n_incomplete
))

cat(sprintf(
  "Min non-zero flux: %.3f mm | Exact zeros: %d | Below 0.1 mm: %d | Below 0.5 mm: %d\n",
  min(peaks_flux$total_flux_short[peaks_flux$total_flux_short > 0]),
  sum(peaks_flux$total_flux_short == 0),
  sum(peaks_flux$total_flux_short < 0.1),
  sum(peaks_flux$total_flux_short < 0.5)
))

# --- Plot: histogram on log scale --------------------------------------------
p <- ggplot(peaks_flux, aes(x = total_flux_short)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5,
                 color = "steelblue4", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.08, length = unit(0.02, "npc")) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500),
    labels = c("0.1", "0.5", "1", "5", "10", "50", "100", "500")
  ) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "b") +
  labs(
    x     = "Total antecedent forcing depth (rain + melt, mm)",
    y     = "Count",
    title = "Distribution of total antecedent WLDAS forcing across POT peaks",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Unregulated sites (n = %d sites, %d peaks with valid flux; %d incomplete windows excluded)",
      n_distinct(peaks_flux$site_no), n_flux_valid, n_incomplete
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(diag_dir, "total_flux_distribution.png"),
  plot = p, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 150
)

p
```

```{r suspect-event-classification-2}
library(tidyverse)

# --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
proj_root <- "/Users/mtalbot/Desktop/GitHub/CoWC_FY26_Enhanced_Impacts/"
data_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_data")
diag_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_diagnostics", "threshold_evaluation")
dir.create(diag_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# --- Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
adaptive <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "pot_peaks_classified_adaptive.rds"))
meta     <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "site_metadata.rds"))

# Deduplicate to one row per peak
adaptive <- adaptive %>%
  distinct(site_no, peak_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Filter to unregulated sites and join drainage area
peaks <- adaptive %>%
  filter(site_no %in% (meta %>% filter(!regulated) %>% pull(site_no))) %>%
  left_join(meta %>% select(site_no, drain_sqkm), by = "site_no")

# Compute q_mm_day: peak_flow (cfs) -> mm/day over basin area
peaks <- peaks %>%
  mutate(q_mm_day = peak_flow * 86400 * 0.0283168 / (drain_sqkm * 1e3))

# Retain only peaks with valid flux and valid q_mm_day
peaks_plot <- peaks %>%
  filter(!is.na(total_flux_short), !is.na(q_mm_day), q_mm_day > 0)

# --- Plot --------------------------------------------------------------------
p <- ggplot(peaks_plot, aes(x = total_flux_short, y = q_mm_day)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8, color = "steelblue4") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
              linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500),
    labels = c("0.1", "0.5", "1", "5", "10", "50", "100", "500")
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100),
    labels = c("0.01", "0.1", "1", "10", "100")
  ) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "bl") +
  labs(
    x        = "Total antecedent forcing depth (rain + melt, mm)",
    y        = "Observed peak flow (mm/day)",
    title    = "Forcing-response relationship across POT peaks",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Unregulated sites (n = %d sites, %d peaks); dashed line = 1:1",
      n_distinct(peaks_plot$site_no), nrow(peaks_plot)
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(diag_dir, "forcing_response_scatter.png"),
  plot = p, width = 7.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 150
)

p
```

# Predictor and response distributions

Note: The goal of this section is to characterize the empirical distributions of the key classification inputs and the flood response variable before any thresholds are applied. This provides the observational foundation for both threshold evaluations and allows the reader to understand the structure of the data — including bimodality, skewness, and cross-variable relationships — that motivates the methodological choices that follow. All distributions should be computed on the full pre-classification peak record (excluding suspect events once the suspect threshold is determined).

## Marginal distributions

```{r marginal-distributions}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
proj_root <- "/Users/mtalbot/Desktop/GitHub/CoWC_FY26_Enhanced_Impacts/"
data_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_data")
diag_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_diagnostics", "threshold_evaluation")
dir.create(diag_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# --- Constants ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Davenport et al. (2020) fixed depth thresholds (mm, 8-day window)
DAVENPORT_RAIN_LOW  <-  5
DAVENPORT_RAIN_HIGH <- 10
DAVENPORT_MELT_LOW  <-  5
DAVENPORT_MELT_HIGH <- 10

# Current adaptive fraction thresholds
SNOW_EM_THRESH <- 0.10
RAIN_EM_THRESH <- 0.95

# --- Load and prepare data ---------------------------------------------------
adaptive <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "pot_peaks_classified_adaptive.rds"))
meta     <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "site_metadata.rds"))

peaks <- adaptive %>%
  distinct(site_no, peak_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(site_no %in% (meta %>% filter(!regulated) %>% pull(site_no))) %>%
  left_join(meta %>% select(site_no, drain_sqkm), by = "site_no") %>%
  mutate(q_mm_day = peak_flow * 86400 * 0.0283168 / (drain_sqkm * 1e3))

n_sites <- n_distinct(peaks$site_no)
n_peaks <- nrow(peaks)

# Peaks with valid flux (non-NA rain_flux_short / melt_flux_short)
peaks_flux <- peaks %>% filter(!is.na(rain_flux_short), !is.na(melt_flux_short))
peaks_frac <- peaks %>% filter(!is.na(rain_frac))
peaks_q    <- peaks %>% filter(!is.na(q_mm_day), q_mm_day > 0)

# --- Shared theme ------------------------------------------------------------
diag_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 8)
  )

# --- Panel 1: Antecedent rainfall depth --------------------------------------
p1 <- ggplot(peaks_flux, aes(x = pmax(rain_flux_short, 0.05))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#E07B39", alpha = 0.5,
                 color = "#C05A1F", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.06, length = unit(0.02, "npc"), color = "#C05A1F") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = DAVENPORT_RAIN_LOW,  linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = DAVENPORT_RAIN_HIGH, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = DAVENPORT_RAIN_LOW,  y = Inf,
           label = "Dav. low\n(5 mm)",  hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3,
           size = 2.8, color = "grey20") +
  annotate("text", x = DAVENPORT_RAIN_HIGH, y = Inf,
           label = "Dav. high\n(10 mm)", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3,
           size = 2.8, color = "grey20") +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500),
    labels = c("0.1", "0.5", "1", "5", "10", "50", "100", "500")
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 300)) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "b") +
  labs(
    title = "Panel 1 — Antecedent rainfall depth",
    x     = "Rainfall depth (mm, adaptive window)",
    y     = "Count"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Panel 2: Antecedent snowmelt depth --------------------------------------
p2 <- ggplot(peaks_flux, aes(x = pmax(melt_flux_short, 0.05))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#5B8DB8", alpha = 0.5,
                 color = "#3A6A9A", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.06, length = unit(0.02, "npc"), color = "#3A6A9A") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = DAVENPORT_MELT_LOW,  linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = DAVENPORT_MELT_HIGH, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = DAVENPORT_MELT_LOW,  y = Inf,
           label = "Dav. low\n(5 mm)",  hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3,
           size = 2.8, color = "grey20") +
  annotate("text", x = DAVENPORT_MELT_HIGH, y = Inf,
           label = "Dav. high\n(10 mm)", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3,
           size = 2.8, color = "grey20") +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500),
    labels = c("0.1", "0.5", "1", "5", "10", "50", "100", "500")
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "b") +
  labs(
    title = "Panel 2 — Antecedent snowmelt depth",
    x     = "Snowmelt depth (mm, adaptive window)",
    y     = "Count"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Panel 3: Rain fraction --------------------------------------------------
p3 <- ggplot(peaks_frac, aes(x = rain_frac)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#6A9E6F", alpha = 0.5,
                 color = "#4A7E4F", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.06, length = unit(0.02, "npc"), color = "#4A7E4F") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = SNOW_EM_THRESH, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = RAIN_EM_THRESH, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = SNOW_EM_THRESH, y = Inf,
           label = "Snow\n(0.10)", hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3,
           size = 2.8, color = "grey20") +
  annotate("text", x = RAIN_EM_THRESH, y = Inf,
           label = "Rain\n(0.95)", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3,
           size = 2.8, color = "grey20") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 300)) +
  labs(
    title = "Panel 3 — Antecedent rain fraction",
    x     = "Rain fraction (adaptive window)",
    y     = "Count"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Panel 4: Observed peak flow (mm/day) ------------------------------------
p4 <- ggplot(peaks_q, aes(x = q_mm_day)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey50", alpha = 0.5,
                 color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.06, length = unit(0.02, "npc"), color = "grey30") +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100),
    labels = c("0.01", "0.1", "1", "10", "100")
  ) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "b") +
  labs(
    title = "Panel 4 — Observed peak flow rate",
    x     = "Peak flow (mm/day)",
    y     = "Count"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Combine with patchwork --------------------------------------------------
fig <- (p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Marginal distributions of classification predictors and flood response",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Unregulated sites (n = %d sites, %d peaks); Davenport thresholds over adaptive window for reference only",
      n_sites, n_peaks
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40")
    )
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(diag_dir, "marginal_distributions.png"),
  plot = fig, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 150
)

fig
```

## Joint distributions
```{r joint-distributions-1}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
proj_root <- "/Users/mtalbot/Desktop/GitHub/CoWC_FY26_Enhanced_Impacts/"
data_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_data")
diag_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_diagnostics", "threshold_evaluation")
dir.create(diag_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# --- Constants ---------------------------------------------------------------
DAVENPORT_RAIN_LOW  <-  5
DAVENPORT_RAIN_HIGH <- 10
DAVENPORT_MELT_LOW  <-  5
DAVENPORT_MELT_HIGH <- 10
SNOW_EM_THRESH      <- 0.10
RAIN_EM_THRESH      <- 0.95
LOG_FLOOR           <- 0.05   # plotting floor for log axes (mm); no methodological meaning

# --- Load and prepare data ---------------------------------------------------
adaptive <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "pot_peaks_classified_adaptive.rds"))
meta     <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "site_metadata.rds"))

peaks <- adaptive %>%
  distinct(site_no, peak_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(site_no %in% (meta %>% filter(!regulated) %>% pull(site_no))) %>%
  left_join(meta %>% select(site_no, drain_sqkm), by = "site_no") %>%
  mutate(q_mm_day = peak_flow * 86400 * 0.0283168 / (drain_sqkm * 1e3))

# Report zero counts before applying log floor
cat(sprintf(
  "rain_flux_short exact zeros : %d\n",
  sum(peaks$rain_flux_short == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
))
cat(sprintf(
  "melt_flux_short exact zeros : %d\n",
  sum(peaks$melt_flux_short == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
))

n_sites <- n_distinct(peaks$site_no)
n_peaks <- nrow(peaks)

# Apply log floor for depth variables
peaks <- peaks %>%
  mutate(
    rain_depth_plot = pmax(rain_flux_short, LOG_FLOOR),
    melt_depth_plot = pmax(melt_flux_short, LOG_FLOOR),
    q_mm_day_plot   = pmax(q_mm_day,        LOG_FLOOR)
  )

# --- Shared theme ------------------------------------------------------------
pt_alpha <- 0.20
pt_size  <- 0.7
pt_color <- "steelblue4"

log_breaks_depth <- c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500)
log_labels_depth <- as.character(log_breaks_depth)
log_breaks_q     <- c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100)
log_labels_q     <- as.character(log_breaks_q)

diag_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 7)
  )

ref_vline <- function(xint) {
  geom_vline(xintercept = xint, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.45)
}
ref_hline <- function(yint) {
  geom_hline(yintercept = yint, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.45)
}
ref_label_v <- function(xint, lab, hjust = 1.1) {
  annotate("text", x = xint, y = Inf, label = lab,
           hjust = hjust, vjust = 1.3, size = 2.4, color = "grey30")
}
ref_label_h <- function(yint, lab, vjust = -0.3) {
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = yint, label = lab,
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = vjust, size = 2.4, color = "grey30")
}

# --- Panel 1: Rainfall depth vs. snowmelt depth ------------------------------
p1_data <- peaks %>% filter(!is.na(rain_depth_plot), !is.na(melt_depth_plot))

p1 <- ggplot(p1_data, aes(x = rain_depth_plot, y = melt_depth_plot)) +
  geom_point(alpha = pt_alpha, size = pt_size, color = pt_color) +
  ref_vline(DAVENPORT_RAIN_LOW)  + ref_label_v(DAVENPORT_RAIN_LOW,  "R=5")  +
  ref_vline(DAVENPORT_RAIN_HIGH) + ref_label_v(DAVENPORT_RAIN_HIGH, "R=10", hjust = -0.1) +
  ref_hline(DAVENPORT_MELT_LOW)  + ref_label_h(DAVENPORT_MELT_LOW,  "M=5")  +
  ref_hline(DAVENPORT_MELT_HIGH) + ref_label_h(DAVENPORT_MELT_HIGH, "M=10", vjust = 1.3) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = log_breaks_depth, labels = log_labels_depth) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = log_breaks_depth, labels = log_labels_depth) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "bl") +
  labs(
    title = "1 — Rainfall depth vs. snowmelt depth",
    x     = "Rainfall depth (mm)",
    y     = "Snowmelt depth (mm)"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Panel 2: Rain fraction vs. antecedent SWE -------------------------------
p2_data <- peaks %>%
  filter(!is.na(rain_frac), !is.na(swe_mean_mm), swe_mean_mm > 0)

p2 <- ggplot(p2_data, aes(x = rain_frac, y = swe_mean_mm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = pt_alpha, size = pt_size, color = pt_color) +
  ref_vline(SNOW_EM_THRESH) + ref_label_v(SNOW_EM_THRESH, "0.10") +
  ref_vline(RAIN_EM_THRESH) + ref_label_v(RAIN_EM_THRESH, "0.95", hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "l") +
  labs(
    title = "2 — Rain fraction vs. antecedent SWE",
    x     = "Rain fraction",
    y     = "Mean antecedent SWE (mm)"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Panel 3: Rain fraction vs. peak flow ------------------------------------
p3_data <- peaks %>% filter(!is.na(rain_frac), !is.na(q_mm_day_plot))

p3 <- ggplot(p3_data, aes(x = rain_frac, y = q_mm_day_plot)) +
  geom_point(alpha = pt_alpha, size = pt_size, color = pt_color) +
  ref_vline(SNOW_EM_THRESH) + ref_label_v(SNOW_EM_THRESH, "0.10") +
  ref_vline(RAIN_EM_THRESH) + ref_label_v(RAIN_EM_THRESH, "0.95", hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = log_breaks_q, labels = log_labels_q) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "l") +
  labs(
    title = "3 — Rain fraction vs. peak flow",
    x     = "Rain fraction",
    y     = "Peak flow (mm/day)"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Panel 4: Rainfall depth vs. rain fraction -------------------------------
p4_data <- peaks %>% filter(!is.na(rain_depth_plot), !is.na(rain_frac))

p4 <- ggplot(p4_data, aes(x = rain_depth_plot, y = rain_frac)) +
  geom_point(alpha = pt_alpha, size = pt_size, color = pt_color) +
  ref_vline(DAVENPORT_RAIN_LOW)  + ref_label_v(DAVENPORT_RAIN_LOW,  "R=5")  +
  ref_vline(DAVENPORT_RAIN_HIGH) + ref_label_v(DAVENPORT_RAIN_HIGH, "R=10", hjust = -0.1) +
  ref_hline(SNOW_EM_THRESH) + ref_label_h(SNOW_EM_THRESH, "0.10") +
  ref_hline(RAIN_EM_THRESH) + ref_label_h(RAIN_EM_THRESH, "0.95", vjust = 1.3) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = log_breaks_depth, labels = log_labels_depth) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "b") +
  labs(
    title = "4 — Rainfall depth vs. rain fraction",
    x     = "Rainfall depth (mm)",
    y     = "Rain fraction"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Panel 5: Snowmelt depth vs. rain fraction -------------------------------
p5_data <- peaks %>% filter(!is.na(melt_depth_plot), !is.na(rain_frac))

p5 <- ggplot(p5_data, aes(x = melt_depth_plot, y = rain_frac)) +
  geom_point(alpha = pt_alpha, size = pt_size, color = pt_color) +
  ref_vline(DAVENPORT_MELT_LOW)  + ref_label_v(DAVENPORT_MELT_LOW,  "M=5")  +
  ref_vline(DAVENPORT_MELT_HIGH) + ref_label_v(DAVENPORT_MELT_HIGH, "M=10", hjust = -0.1) +
  ref_hline(SNOW_EM_THRESH) + ref_label_h(SNOW_EM_THRESH, "0.10") +
  ref_hline(RAIN_EM_THRESH) + ref_label_h(RAIN_EM_THRESH, "0.95", vjust = 1.3) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = log_breaks_depth, labels = log_labels_depth) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "b") +
  labs(
    title = "5 — Snowmelt depth vs. rain fraction",
    x     = "Snowmelt depth (mm)",
    y     = "Rain fraction"
  ) +
  diag_theme

# --- Combine -----------------------------------------------------------------
fig <- (p1 + p2 + p3) / (p4 + p5 + plot_spacer()) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Joint distributions of classification predictors and flood response",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Unregulated sites (n = %d sites, %d peaks); Davenport thresholds shown for reference only",
      n_sites, n_peaks
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40")
    )
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(diag_dir, "joint_distributions.png"),
  plot = fig, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 150
)

fig
```


# Depth threshold evaluation
Here's a summary of what was tried and why each approach was abandoned. The chunks refer to since-deleted diagnostic code:
* Strategy 1 — Weighted inter-class separation metric (chunk 1). A 50×50 grid search over rainfall and snowmelt depth thresholds (0.5–25mm), maximizing the mean absolute difference in per-site median streamflow (mm/day) between rainfall- and snowmelt-classified events, with a sqrt(n/n_max) penalty for thresholds that produced few eligible sites. The objective was reasonable but the metric is essentially asking whether the depth thresholds produce hydrologically meaningful class separation. It found an optimum but there's no guarantee the optimum is stable, interpretable, or that it generalizes across site types. The Davenport reference points performed comparably, undermining the case for optimization.
* Strategy 2 — Minimize unclassified fraction subject to a separation floor (chunk 2). Reframed the problem as a coverage-vs-purity tradeoff: find the threshold combination that leaves the fewest events unclassified, conditional on inter-class separation remaining above 25%, 50%, or 75% of its grid maximum. This is a more defensible framing but still anchored to the same separation metric, with the same weakness. It also introduced a reference to target_k and boundary variables (bnd_lines, B2_INTERCEPT_BASE, etc.) that are undefined in chunk 2 but appear in chunk 3, suggesting the chunks were developed in an overlapping or nonlinear order.
* Strategy 3 — Count calibration to adaptive classification (chunk 3). Fixed the rainfall threshold at 1.0mm (derived from agreement maximization with the adaptive GMM classification) and searched for a snowmelt threshold M that minimized Euclidean distance between depth-classified counts and adaptive-classified counts in snowmelt × ROS space. This is explicitly not a process-based criterion — it's trying to make the depth scheme mimic the adaptive scheme's marginal distributions, which is circular if the goal is an independent fixed-threshold alternative. The script references target_k, bnd_lines, and peaks_target that are undefined within the chunk, so it also appears to have been written in conjunction with chunk 4.
* Strategy 4 — GMM boundary adjustment in rain_frac × SWE space (chunk 4). Shifted the B2 boundary (the ROS/rainfall dividing line in rain_frac vs. log10(SWE+1) space) by a scaling factor k to recover more sites with ≥20 ROS events, targeting the minimum k satisfying both ROS and snowmelt viability. This moves away from depth thresholds entirely and back into the adaptive predictor space, essentially acknowledging that depth thresholds can't recover the ROS class at adequate sample sizes.

Net conclusion: None of these approaches produced a fixed threshold scheme that is simultaneously: (a) process-motivated rather than circular, (b) capable of recovering ROS as a viable class at enough sites, and (c) clearly superior to or meaningfully different from Davenport's original thresholds. The predictor-space (rain_frac) adaptive scheme already does the classification well; the problem was justifying the thresholds within that scheme, not finding a depth-based alternative.

Proposed path forward — GPD sensitivity as the optimization criterion
The core idea is right: rather than optimizing thresholds against a predictor-space or count-matching criterion, evaluate the thresholds against how well the resulting GPD fits behave statistically at the population level. This is more directly connected to the FFA objective and avoids the circularity problem.

```{r depth-threshold-optimization-test}
# =============================================================================
# Depth Threshold Optimization — GPD Mixture vs. Single-Sample Q100
#
# Objective: find the (rain_thresh, snow_thresh) pair that maximizes the
# mean across eligible sites of:
#
#   Q_mixture(RI=100) - Q_singlesample(RI=100)
#
# where both are GPD-based fits using the existing functions.R machinery.
#
# Classification rule (depth decision tree):
#   rainfall  : rain_depth >= rain_thresh  AND  melt_depth <  snow_thresh
#   snowmelt  : melt_depth >= snow_thresh  AND  rain_depth <  rain_thresh
#   ROS       : rain_depth >= rain_thresh  AND  melt_depth >= snow_thresh
#   (unclassified = below both thresholds; excluded from fitting)
#
# Eligibility: unregulated sites where at least TWO flood types each have
# >= MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE events after classification. Sites with only one
# qualifying type are excluded (no genuine mixture possible).
#
# Single-sample GPD: fit to all classified (non-unclassified) peaks at site.
#
# Grid: rain_thresh and snow_thresh each from 1 to 25 mm, step 1 mm (625
# combinations).
#
# Reference points: Davenport et al. (2020) low (5/5) and high (10/10).
#
# Outputs saved to: _diagnostics/threshold_evaluation/depth_thresholds/gpd_objective/
# =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(lmomco)
library(patchwork)

# Pin namespace collisions (mclust, MASS may be loaded in session)
map     <- purrr::map
map_dfr <- purrr::map_dfr

# --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
proj_root <- "/Users/mtalbot/Desktop/GitHub/CoWC_FY26_Enhanced_Impacts/"
data_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_data")
diag_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_diagnostics", "threshold_evaluation",
                       "depth_thresholds", "gpd_objective")
dir.create(diag_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

source(file.path(proj_root, "functions.R"))

# --- Constants ---------------------------------------------------------------
MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE     <- 20L
TARGET_RI           <- 100       # single return period for now
DAVENPORT_LOW       <- 5.0
DAVENPORT_HIGH      <- 10.0

# --- Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
adaptive <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "pot_peaks_classified_adaptive.rds"))
meta     <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "site_metadata.rds"))

unreg_sites <- meta %>% filter(!regulated) %>% pull(site_no)

# One row per peak; retain depth fluxes and pot threshold
peaks <- adaptive %>%
  distinct(site_no, peak_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(site_no %in% unreg_sites) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rain_flux_short), !is.na(melt_flux_short),
         !is.na(peak_flow), !is.na(peak_date),
         !is.na(pot_threshold_cfs)) %>%
  mutate(peak_date = as.Date(peak_date)) %>%
  rename(rain_depth = rain_flux_short,
         melt_depth = melt_flux_short) %>%
  dplyr::select(site_no, peak_id, peak_date, peak_flow,
                pot_threshold_cfs, rain_depth, melt_depth)

cat(sprintf("Peaks loaded: %d across %d unregulated sites\n",
            nrow(peaks), n_distinct(peaks$site_no)))

peaks_by_site <- split(peaks, peaks$site_no)

# --- Helper: invert mixture SF at a single RI --------------------------------
# Scalar version of mixture_curve() — avoids overhead of building full curve.
mixture_quantile_at_ri <- function(fits, ri) {
  target <- 1 / ri
  lb     <- min(sapply(fits, function(f) f$mu), na.rm = TRUE)

  # Build upper bound by doubling until mixture_sf drops below target
  ub <- max(sapply(fits, function(f) gpd_quantile(target, f)), na.rm = TRUE) * 2
  ub <- max(ub, lb + 1)
  for (i in seq_len(40)) {
    if (isTRUE(mixture_sf(ub, fits) < target)) break
    ub <- ub * 2
  }

  f_lb <- mixture_sf(lb, fits) - target
  f_ub <- mixture_sf(ub, fits) - target
  if (is.na(f_lb) || is.na(f_ub) || sign(f_lb) == sign(f_ub)) return(NA_real_)

  tryCatch(
    uniroot(function(x) mixture_sf(x, fits) - target,
            lower = lb, upper = ub, tol = 0.1)$root,
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )
}

# --- Core evaluation function ------------------------------------------------
evaluate_thresholds <- function(rain_thresh, snow_thresh) {

  site_results <- purrr::map_dfr(peaks_by_site, function(sp) {
    mu <- sp$pot_threshold_cfs[1]

    # Classify
    sp <- sp %>%
      mutate(depth_class = case_when(
        rain_depth >= rain_thresh & melt_depth <  snow_thresh ~ "rainfall",
        melt_depth >= snow_thresh & rain_depth <  rain_thresh ~ "snowmelt",
        rain_depth >= rain_thresh & melt_depth >= snow_thresh ~ "ROS",
        TRUE                                                  ~ "unclassified"
      ))

    # Count by type
    type_counts <- sp %>%
      filter(depth_class != "unclassified") %>%
      dplyr::count(depth_class)

    # Require at least two types with MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE
    eligible_types <- type_counts %>%
      filter(n >= MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE) %>%
      pull(depth_class)

    if (length(eligible_types) < 2) return(NULL)

    # Fit per-type GPDs
    type_fits <- purrr::map(eligible_types, function(tp) {
      sub <- sp %>% filter(depth_class == tp)
      fit_gpd(sub$peak_flow, sub$peak_date, mu_threshold = mu,
              min_n = MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE)
    })
    names(type_fits) <- eligible_types

    # Drop any NULL fits (degenerate L-moments)
    type_fits <- Filter(Negate(is.null), type_fits)
    if (length(type_fits) < 2) return(NULL)

    # Single-sample GPD: all classified (non-unclassified) peaks
    all_classified <- sp %>% filter(depth_class != "unclassified")
    ss_fit <- fit_gpd(all_classified$peak_flow, all_classified$peak_date,
                      mu_threshold = mu, min_n = MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE)
    if (is.null(ss_fit)) return(NULL)

    # Q100: mixture and single-sample
    q_mix <- mixture_quantile_at_ri(type_fits, TARGET_RI)
    q_ss  <- gpd_quantile(1 / TARGET_RI, ss_fit)

    if (is.na(q_mix) || is.na(q_ss) || q_ss <= 0) return(NULL)

    tibble(
      site_no        = sp$site_no[1],
      n_types        = length(type_fits),
      q_mixture      = q_mix,
      q_singlesample = q_ss,
      delta_q        = q_mix - q_ss
    )
  })

  if (nrow(site_results) == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      mean_delta_q   = NA_real_,
      median_delta_q = NA_real_,
      n_eligible     = 0L
    ))
  }

  tibble(
    mean_delta_q   = mean(site_results$delta_q,   na.rm = TRUE),
    median_delta_q = median(site_results$delta_q, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_eligible     = nrow(site_results)
  )
}

# --- Grid search -------------------------------------------------------------
thresh_seq <- seq(1, 25, by = 1)
grid       <- expand.grid(rain_thresh = thresh_seq, snow_thresh = thresh_seq)

cat(sprintf("Grid size: %d combinations\n", nrow(grid)))
cat("Running grid search (this may take a few minutes)...\n")

t0 <- proc.time()

results <- purrr::map2_dfr(
  grid$rain_thresh,
  grid$snow_thresh,
  function(r, s) {
    res <- evaluate_thresholds(r, s)
    res %>% mutate(rain_thresh = r, snow_thresh = s)
  }
) %>%
  dplyr::select(rain_thresh, snow_thresh,
                mean_delta_q, median_delta_q, n_eligible)

elapsed <- proc.time() - t0
cat(sprintf("Grid search complete: %.1f seconds\n", elapsed["elapsed"]))

# --- Report ------------------------------------------------------------------
opt_mean <- results %>%
  filter(!is.na(mean_delta_q)) %>%
  slice_max(mean_delta_q, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

opt_median <- results %>%
  filter(!is.na(median_delta_q)) %>%
  slice_max(median_delta_q, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

cat(sprintf(
  "\nOptimal (mean delta Q100):\n  Rain: %g mm | Snow: %g mm\n  Mean delta: %.2f cfs | Eligible sites: %d\n",
  opt_mean$rain_thresh, opt_mean$snow_thresh,
  opt_mean$mean_delta_q, opt_mean$n_eligible
))

cat(sprintf(
  "\nOptimal (median delta Q100):\n  Rain: %g mm | Snow: %g mm\n  Median delta: %.2f cfs | Eligible sites: %d\n",
  opt_median$rain_thresh, opt_median$snow_thresh,
  opt_median$median_delta_q, opt_median$n_eligible
))

# Davenport reference points
for (dav in list(c(DAVENPORT_LOW, DAVENPORT_LOW), c(DAVENPORT_HIGH, DAVENPORT_HIGH))) {
  ref <- results %>%
    filter(rain_thresh == dav[1], snow_thresh == dav[2])
  cat(sprintf(
    "\nDavenport (%g/%g mm): mean_delta=%.2f, median_delta=%.2f, n_eligible=%d\n",
    dav[1], dav[2],
    ref$mean_delta_q, ref$median_delta_q, ref$n_eligible
  ))
}

# Save results table
saveRDS(results, file.path(diag_dir, "grid_results.rds"))

# --- Figures -----------------------------------------------------------------
heatmap_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid  = element_blank(),
    axis.text   = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title  = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8)
  )

shared_xy <- list(
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 25, 5)),
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 25, 5)),
  labs(x = "Rainfall depth threshold (mm)",
       y = "Snowmelt depth threshold (mm)")
)

dav_points <- list(
  geom_point(
    data = tibble(
      x = c(DAVENPORT_LOW,  DAVENPORT_HIGH),
      y = c(DAVENPORT_LOW,  DAVENPORT_HIGH),
      lbl = c("Dav. low\n(5/5)", "Dav. high\n(10/10)")
    ),
    aes(x = x, y = y),
    shape = 4, size = 3, color = "white", stroke = 1.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ),
  geom_text(
    data = tibble(
      x = c(DAVENPORT_LOW,  DAVENPORT_HIGH),
      y = c(DAVENPORT_LOW,  DAVENPORT_HIGH),
      lbl = c("Dav. low\n(5/5)", "Dav. high\n(10/10)")
    ),
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = lbl),
    hjust = -0.15, vjust = 0.5, size = 2.3, color = "white",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  )
)

opt_point <- function(opt_row, color = "yellow") {
  list(
    geom_point(
      data = opt_row,
      aes(x = rain_thresh, y = snow_thresh),
      shape = 21, size = 3.5, fill = color, color = "black", stroke = 0.9,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ),
    geom_text(
      data = opt_row,
      aes(x = rain_thresh, y = snow_thresh,
          label = sprintf("Opt\n(%g, %g)", rain_thresh, snow_thresh)),
      hjust = -0.15, vjust = 0.5, size = 2.5, color = color,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    )
  )
}

# Figure 1: Mean delta Q100 heatmap
p_mean <- ggplot(results %>% filter(!is.na(mean_delta_q)),
                 aes(x = rain_thresh, y = snow_thresh, fill = mean_delta_q)) +
  geom_tile() +
  opt_point(opt_mean) +
  dav_points +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdYlBu", direction = 1,
                       name = "Mean delta\nQ100 (cfs)",
                       na.value = "grey80") +
  shared_xy +
  labs(
    title    = "Mean [Q_mixture(100) - Q_singlesample(100)] across eligible sites",
    subtitle = sprintf("Optimal: rain=%g mm, snow=%g mm | mean delta=%.2f cfs | n=%d sites",
                       opt_mean$rain_thresh, opt_mean$snow_thresh,
                       opt_mean$mean_delta_q, opt_mean$n_eligible)
  ) +
  heatmap_theme

# Figure 2: Eligible site count heatmap
p_sites <- ggplot(results,
                  aes(x = rain_thresh, y = snow_thresh, fill = n_eligible)) +
  geom_tile() +
  opt_point(opt_mean) +
  dav_points +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Eligible\nsites", option = "magma",
                       direction = -1) +
  shared_xy +

    title    = "Number of eligible sites (>= 2 types with >= 20 events)",
    subtitle = sprintf("Max eligible: %d", max(results$n_eligible, na.rm = TRUE))
  ) +
  heatmap_theme

# Figure 3: Sensitivity curves at optimum
sens_rain <- results %>%
  filter(snow_thresh == opt_mean$snow_thresh, !is.na(mean_delta_q)) %>%

sens_snow <- results %>%
  filter(rain_thresh == opt_mean$rain_thresh, !is.na(mean_delta_q)) %>%

p_sens <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = sens_rain,
            aes(x = rain_thresh, y = mean_delta_q,

# Figure 4: Median delta Q100 heatmap (robustness check)

ggsave(file.path(diag_dir, "mean_delta_q100_heatmap.png"),
       plot = p_mean,       width = 7,  height = 5.5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r depth-threshold-optimization-full}
# =============================================================================
# Depth Threshold Optimization — GPD Mixture vs. Single-Sample, Multi-RI v2
#
# Objective: find the (rain_thresh, snow_thresh) pair that maximizes the
# unweighted mean of per-RI mean relative deltas across upper-tail RIs:
#
#   mean_rel_delta(RI) = mean over eligible sites at that RI of
#                        [ (Q_mix(RI) - Q_ss(RI)) / Q_ss(RI) ]
#   objective = mean over RIs of mean_rel_delta(RI)
#
# Key changes from v1:
#   - RIs restricted to upper tail: 10, 25, 50, 100 yr (drops 2 and 5 yr,
#     which measured partitioning mechanics near the distribution center
#     rather than tail behavior, and dominated the v1 aggregate)
#   - Per-RI means computed independently over sites eligible at that RI
#     (removes the all-RIs-finite requirement that reduced eligible n to
#     14 sites and created a severe selection bias in v1)
#   - Aggregate = mean of per-RI means (not mean of per-site sums), so
#     RI-specific site dropouts do not distort the aggregate
#
# Classification rule (depth decision tree):
#   rainfall  : rain_depth >= rain_thresh  AND  melt_depth <  snow_thresh
#   snowmelt  : melt_depth >= snow_thresh  AND  rain_depth <  rain_thresh
#   ROS       : rain_depth >= rain_thresh  AND  melt_depth >= snow_thresh
#   unclassified : below both thresholds — excluded from fitting
#
# Eligibility (per site, per RI): unregulated site with >= MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE
# events in at least TWO flood types AND finite mixture + single-sample
# quantiles at that specific RI. Eligibility is assessed per RI independently.
#
# Grid: rain_thresh and snow_thresh each from 1 to 25 mm, step 1 mm (625
# combinations).
#
# Outputs:
#   grid_results_multiRI_v2.rds  — full grid table
#   aggregate_heatmap.png        — primary objective
#   eligible_sites_heatmap.png   — mean n eligible sites across RIs
#   per_ri_heatmaps.png          — small-multiple heatmap, one panel per RI
#   sensitivity_curves.png       — 1D slices through optimum
#   depth_threshold_multiRI_v2.png — combined figure
#
# All saved to:
#   _diagnostics/threshold_evaluation/depth_thresholds/gpd_objective_multiRI_v2/
# =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(lmomco)
library(patchwork)

# Pin namespace collisions
map     <- purrr::map
map_dfr <- purrr::map_dfr

# --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
proj_root <- "/Users/mtalbot/Desktop/GitHub/CoWC_FY26_Enhanced_Impacts/"
data_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_data")
diag_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_diagnostics", "threshold_evaluation",
                       "depth_thresholds", "gpd_objective_multiRI_v2")
dir.create(diag_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

source(file.path(proj_root, "functions.R"))

# --- Constants ---------------------------------------------------------------
MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE <- 20L
TARGET_RIS      <- c(10, 25, 50, 100)   # upper tail only; drops 2 and 5 yr
DAVENPORT_LOW   <- 5.0
DAVENPORT_HIGH  <- 10.0

# --- Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
adaptive <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "pot_peaks_classified_adaptive.rds"))
meta     <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "site_metadata.rds"))

unreg_sites <- meta %>% filter(!regulated) %>% pull(site_no)

peaks <- adaptive %>%
  distinct(site_no, peak_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(site_no %in% unreg_sites) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rain_flux_short), !is.na(melt_flux_short),
         !is.na(peak_flow), !is.na(peak_date),
         !is.na(pot_threshold_cfs)) %>%
  mutate(peak_date = as.Date(peak_date)) %>%
  rename(rain_depth = rain_flux_short,
         melt_depth = melt_flux_short) %>%
  dplyr::select(site_no, peak_id, peak_date, peak_flow,
                pot_threshold_cfs, rain_depth, melt_depth)

cat(sprintf("Peaks loaded: %d across %d unregulated sites\n",
            nrow(peaks), n_distinct(peaks$site_no)))

peaks_by_site <- split(peaks, peaks$site_no)

# --- Helper: invert mixture SF at a single RI --------------------------------
mixture_quantile_at_ri <- function(fits, ri) {
  target <- 1 / ri
  lb     <- min(sapply(fits, function(f) f$mu), na.rm = TRUE)
  ub     <- max(sapply(fits, function(f) gpd_quantile(target, f)),
                na.rm = TRUE) * 2
  ub     <- max(ub, lb + 1)
  for (i in seq_len(40)) {
    if (isTRUE(mixture_sf(ub, fits) < target)) break
    ub <- ub * 2
  }
  f_lb <- mixture_sf(lb, fits) - target
  f_ub <- mixture_sf(ub, fits) - target
  if (is.na(f_lb) || is.na(f_ub) || sign(f_lb) == sign(f_ub)) return(NA_real_)
  tryCatch(
    uniroot(function(x) mixture_sf(x, fits) - target,
            lower = lb, upper = ub, tol = 0.1)$root,
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )
}

# --- Core evaluation function ------------------------------------------------
# Returns one row per eligible site with per-RI relative deltas (NA allowed).
# A site is included if it has >= 2 fitted types and a valid single-sample fit.
# Each RI's relative delta is NA if mixture inversion fails at that RI.
# Aggregation uses per-RI means over finite sites — eligibility assessed per RI.
evaluate_thresholds <- function(rain_thresh, snow_thresh) {

  site_results <- purrr::map_dfr(peaks_by_site, function(sp) {
    mu <- sp$pot_threshold_cfs[1]

    # Classify
    sp <- sp %>%
      mutate(depth_class = case_when(
        rain_depth >= rain_thresh & melt_depth <  snow_thresh ~ "rainfall",
        melt_depth >= snow_thresh & rain_depth <  rain_thresh ~ "snowmelt",
        rain_depth >= rain_thresh & melt_depth >= snow_thresh ~ "ROS",
        TRUE                                                  ~ "unclassified"
      ))

    # Require >= 2 types with MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE
    eligible_types <- sp %>%
      filter(depth_class != "unclassified") %>%
      dplyr::count(depth_class) %>%
      filter(n >= MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE) %>%
      pull(depth_class)

    if (length(eligible_types) < 2) return(NULL)

    # Per-type GPD fits
    type_fits <- purrr::map(eligible_types, function(tp) {
      sub <- sp %>% filter(depth_class == tp)
      fit_gpd(sub$peak_flow, sub$peak_date,
              mu_threshold = mu, min_n = MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE)
    })
    names(type_fits) <- eligible_types
    type_fits <- Filter(Negate(is.null), type_fits)
    if (length(type_fits) < 2) return(NULL)

    # Single-sample GPD
    all_classified <- sp %>% filter(depth_class != "unclassified")
    ss_fit <- fit_gpd(all_classified$peak_flow, all_classified$peak_date,
                      mu_threshold = mu, min_n = MIN_TYPE_SAMPLE)
    if (is.null(ss_fit)) return(NULL)

    # Per-RI relative delta — NA allowed; eligibility assessed per RI
    rel_deltas <- purrr::map_dbl(TARGET_RIS, function(ri) {
      q_mix <- mixture_quantile_at_ri(type_fits, ri)
      q_ss  <- gpd_quantile(1 / ri, ss_fit)
      if (is.na(q_mix) || is.na(q_ss) || q_ss <= 0) return(NA_real_)
      (q_mix - q_ss) / q_ss
    })
    names(rel_deltas) <- paste0("rel_delta_", TARGET_RIS)

    # Include site as long as at least one RI is finite
    if (all(is.na(rel_deltas))) return(NULL)

    bind_cols(
      tibble(site_no = sp$site_no[1], n_types = length(type_fits)),
      as_tibble(as.list(rel_deltas))
    )
  })

  ri_col_names <- paste0("rel_delta_", TARGET_RIS)

  if (nrow(site_results) == 0) {
    base    <- tibble(mean_agg = NA_real_, mean_n_eligible = 0L)
    ri_cols <- setNames(
      as.list(rep(NA_real_, length(TARGET_RIS))),
      paste0("mean_rel_delta_", TARGET_RIS)
    )
    n_cols <- setNames(
      as.list(rep(0L, length(TARGET_RIS))),
      paste0("n_eligible_", TARGET_RIS)
    )
    return(bind_cols(base, as_tibble(ri_cols), as_tibble(n_cols)))
  }

  # Per-RI mean over sites with finite values at that RI
  ri_means <- purrr::map_dfc(TARGET_RIS, function(ri) {
    col  <- paste0("rel_delta_", ri)
    vals <- site_results[[col]]
    tibble(
      !!paste0("mean_rel_delta_", ri) := mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
      !!paste0("n_eligible_",     ri) := sum(!is.na(vals))
    )
  })

  # Aggregate = unweighted mean of per-RI means (only over RIs with >=1 site)
  per_ri_means <- unlist(ri_means[, paste0("mean_rel_delta_", TARGET_RIS)])
  mean_agg     <- mean(per_ri_means, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Mean eligible n across RIs (for heatmap)
  per_ri_n        <- unlist(ri_means[, paste0("n_eligible_", TARGET_RIS)])
  mean_n_eligible <- mean(per_ri_n, na.rm = TRUE)

  bind_cols(
    tibble(mean_agg = mean_agg, mean_n_eligible = mean_n_eligible),
    ri_means
  )
}

# --- Grid search -------------------------------------------------------------
thresh_seq <- seq(1, 25, by = 1)
grid       <- expand.grid(rain_thresh = thresh_seq, snow_thresh = thresh_seq)

cat(sprintf("Grid size: %d combinations | RIs: %s\n",
            nrow(grid), paste(TARGET_RIS, collapse = ", ")))
cat("Running grid search...\n")

t0 <- proc.time()

results <- purrr::map2_dfr(
  grid$rain_thresh,
  grid$snow_thresh,
  function(r, s) {
    res <- evaluate_thresholds(r, s)
    bind_cols(tibble(rain_thresh = r, snow_thresh = s), res)
  }
)

elapsed <- proc.time() - t0
cat(sprintf("Grid search complete: %.1f seconds\n", elapsed["elapsed"]))

# --- Report optima -----------------------------------------------------------
opt <- results %>%
  filter(!is.na(mean_agg)) %>%
  slice_max(mean_agg, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

cat(sprintf(
  "\nOptimal (mean of per-RI means):\n  Rain: %g mm | Snow: %g mm\n  Mean agg: %.4f | Mean eligible sites: %.1f\n",
  opt$rain_thresh, opt$snow_thresh, opt$mean_agg, opt$mean_n_eligible
))

for (dav in list(c(DAVENPORT_LOW, DAVENPORT_LOW),
                 c(DAVENPORT_HIGH, DAVENPORT_HIGH))) {
  ref <- results %>%
    filter(rain_thresh == dav[1], snow_thresh == dav[2])
  cat(sprintf(
    "Davenport (%g/%g mm): mean_agg=%.4f, mean_n_eligible=%.1f\n",
    dav[1], dav[2], ref$mean_agg, ref$mean_n_eligible
  ))
}

# Per-RI optimum summary
cat("\nPer-RI optima:\n")
for (ri in TARGET_RIS) {
  col   <- paste0("mean_rel_delta_", ri)
  n_col <- paste0("n_eligible_", ri)
  ri_opt <- results %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) %>%
    slice_max(.data[[col]], n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("  RI=%3d yr: rain=%g mm, snow=%g mm, mean_rel_delta=%.4f, n=%d\n",
              ri, ri_opt$rain_thresh, ri_opt$snow_thresh,
              ri_opt[[col]], ri_opt[[n_col]]))
}

saveRDS(results, file.path(diag_dir, "grid_results_multiRI_v2.rds"))

# --- Shared plot elements ----------------------------------------------------

# --- Figure 1: Aggregate heatmap ---------------------------------------------
p_agg <- ggplot(results %>% filter(!is.na(mean_agg)),
```

# Rainfall fraction threshold evaluation
```{r rainfall-fraction-thresholds-1}
# =============================================================================
# Rainfall Fraction Threshold Evaluation — Joint GMM in rain_frac x SWE space
#
# NOTE: GMM is used here as a boundary-identification tool in a specific 2D
# subspace (rain_frac x log10(SWE + 1)), not as the classification engine
# directly. Prior work found GMM non-viable as a classifier due to class
# imbalance and continuous process distributions; that finding does not
# preclude this more constrained use. Panel 2 of the joint distributions
# figure showed sufficient visual structure in this subspace to justify
# proceeding.
# =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(mclust)
library(patchwork)

# --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------
proj_root <- "/Users/mtalbot/Desktop/GitHub/CoWC_FY26_Enhanced_Impacts/"
data_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_data")
diag_dir  <- file.path(proj_root, "_diagnostics", "threshold_evaluation",
                       "gmm_rain_frac_swe")
dir.create(diag_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# --- Constants ---------------------------------------------------------------
SNOW_EM_THRESH <- 0.10
RAIN_EM_THRESH <- 0.95
SWE_LOG_OFFSET <- 1.0   # mm; added before log10 to handle near-zero SWE

# Covariance structures to include in BIC plot
BIC_MODELS <- c("EEE", "VVV", "EEV")

# Flood type colors (consistent with pipeline palette)
type_colors <- c(
  "rainfall"     = "#E07B39",
  "snowmelt"     = "#5B8DB8",
  "ROS"          = "#6A9E6F",
  "unclassified" = "grey70"
)

# --- Load and prepare data ---------------------------------------------------
adaptive <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "pot_peaks_classified_adaptive.rds"))
meta     <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "site_metadata.rds"))

peaks_raw <- adaptive %>%
  distinct(site_no, peak_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(site_no %in% (meta %>% filter(!regulated) %>% pull(site_no)))

# GMM fitting subset: require valid rain_frac and swe_mean_mm
gmm_data <- peaks_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(rain_frac), !is.na(swe_mean_mm)) %>%
  mutate(swe_log = log10(swe_mean_mm + SWE_LOG_OFFSET))

cat(sprintf("Peaks available for GMM: %d (of %d total)\n",
            nrow(gmm_data), nrow(peaks_raw)))
cat(sprintf("Peaks excluded (NA rain_frac or swe_mean_mm): %d\n",
            nrow(peaks_raw) - nrow(gmm_data)))

# Scale features to zero mean / unit variance before fitting
rain_frac_mean <- mean(gmm_data$rain_frac)
rain_frac_sd   <- sd(gmm_data$rain_frac)
swe_log_mean   <- mean(gmm_data$swe_log)
swe_log_sd     <- sd(gmm_data$swe_log)

gmm_data <- gmm_data %>%
  mutate(
    rain_frac_scaled = (rain_frac - rain_frac_mean) / rain_frac_sd,
    swe_log_scaled   = (swe_log   - swe_log_mean)   / swe_log_sd
  )

X <- gmm_data %>% select(rain_frac_scaled, swe_log_scaled) %>% as.matrix()

# --- Fit GMM: G = 2, 3, 4 with restricted model set -------------------------
cat("\nFitting GMM solutions (G = 2, 3, 4)...\n")

fit <- Mclust(X, G = 2:4, modelNames = BIC_MODELS, verbose = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("\nBIC-selected solution: G = %d, model = %s\n",
            fit$G, fit$modelName))
cat(sprintf("BIC values:\n"))
print(fit$BIC)

# Per-component summary in original units
gmm_data <- gmm_data %>%
  mutate(gmm_component = fit$classification)

comp_summary <- gmm_data %>%
  group_by(gmm_component) %>%
  summarise(
    n            = dplyr::n(),
    rain_frac_med = median(rain_frac),
    swe_med_mm    = median(swe_mean_mm),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
cat("\nComponent summary (original units):\n")
print(comp_summary)

# Order components by median rain_frac ascending — used for boundary
# extraction and classification change analysis
comp_order <- order(comp_summary$rain_frac_med)

# --- BIC plot ----------------------------------------------------------------
# mclust BIC object is a matrix [G x models]; extract carefully
bic_matrix <- fit$BIC  # class "mclustBIC", underlying matrix

bic_df <- as.data.frame(unclass(bic_matrix)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("G") %>%
  mutate(G = as.integer(G)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-G, names_to = "model", values_to = "BIC") %>%
  filter(!is.na(BIC), model %in% BIC_MODELS)

p_bic <- ggplot(bic_df, aes(x = G, y = BIC, color = model, group = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:4) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "Covariance") +
  labs(
    title    = "GMM BIC by number of components and covariance structure",
    subtitle = sprintf("Features: rain_frac x log10(SWE + 1), scaled; n = %d peaks",
                       nrow(gmm_data)),
    x        = "Number of components (G)",
    y        = "BIC"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave(file.path(diag_dir, "gmm_bic_curve.png"),
       plot = p_bic, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 150)

# --- Boundary extraction -----------------------------------------------------
# Equal-posterior boundary: for each pair of adjacent components (ordered by
# median rain_frac), find the rain_frac value at which P(A) = P(B) = 0.5
# evaluated at a specified SWE value.
#
# Boundary evaluated at two physically motivated SWE points:
#   low-SWE  : median SWE of flood_type_raw == "rainfall" events
#   high-SWE : median SWE of flood_type_raw == "snowmelt" events

swe_low_mm  <- median(gmm_data$swe_mean_mm[gmm_data$flood_type_raw == "rainfall"],
                      na.rm = TRUE)
swe_high_mm <- median(gmm_data$swe_mean_mm[gmm_data$flood_type_raw == "snowmelt"],
                      na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("\nBoundary evaluation points:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Low-SWE  (median rainfall SWE)  : %.2f mm\n", swe_low_mm))
cat(sprintf("  High-SWE (median snowmelt SWE)  : %.2f mm\n", swe_high_mm))

# Function: given a fixed SWE (mm, original units), compute posterior
# probabilities across a rain_frac grid and find equal-posterior crossings
find_boundary_rain_frac <- function(fit, swe_mm_fixed,
                                    rain_frac_mean, rain_frac_sd,
                                    swe_log_mean, swe_log_sd,
                                    swe_log_offset = 1.0,
                                    n_grid = 2000) {
  rf_grid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_grid)

  swe_log_fixed  <- log10(swe_mm_fixed + swe_log_offset)
  rf_scaled      <- (rf_grid - rain_frac_mean) / rain_frac_sd
  swe_scaled     <- rep((swe_log_fixed - swe_log_mean) / swe_log_sd, n_grid)

  grid_mat <- cbind(rf_scaled, swe_scaled)
  probs    <- predict(fit, newdata = grid_mat)$z  # n_grid x G matrix

  # Order components by median rain_frac (ascending) for consistent labeling
  comp_order <- order(comp_summary$rain_frac_med)

  boundaries <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(ncol(probs) - 1)) {
    ca <- comp_order[i]
    cb <- comp_order[i + 1]
    diff_probs <- probs[, ca] - probs[, cb]
    sign_changes <- which(diff(sign(diff_probs)) != 0)
    if (length(sign_changes) > 0) {
      # Linear interpolation to refine crossing
      idx <- sign_changes[1]
      rf_cross <- rf_grid[idx] +
        (rf_grid[idx + 1] - rf_grid[idx]) *
        abs(diff_probs[idx]) / (abs(diff_probs[idx]) + abs(diff_probs[idx + 1]))
      boundaries[[paste0("C", ca, "_C", cb)]] <- rf_cross
    }
  }
  boundaries
}

bounds_low  <- find_boundary_rain_frac(fit, swe_low_mm,
                                        rain_frac_mean, rain_frac_sd,
                                        swe_log_mean,   swe_log_sd)
bounds_high <- find_boundary_rain_frac(fit, swe_high_mm,
                                        rain_frac_mean, rain_frac_sd,
                                        swe_log_mean,   swe_log_sd)

cat("\nGMM-derived rain_frac boundaries:\n")
cat("  At low-SWE (rainfall median):\n")
for (nm in names(bounds_low))
  cat(sprintf("    %s : rain_frac = %.3f\n", nm, bounds_low[[nm]]))
cat("  At high-SWE (snowmelt median):\n")
for (nm in names(bounds_high))
  cat(sprintf("    %s : rain_frac = %.3f\n", nm, bounds_high[[nm]]))

cat(sprintf("\nCurrent thresholds: SNOW_EM_THRESH = %.2f, RAIN_EM_THRESH = %.2f\n",
            SNOW_EM_THRESH, RAIN_EM_THRESH))

# --- Component ellipse overlay (uncolored) -----------------------------------
# Helper: generate ellipse polygon for a single GMM component in scaled space,
# then back-transform to original units for plotting
make_ellipse <- function(mu, sigma, n_sd = 2, n_pts = 200) {
  theta  <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n_pts)
  circle <- rbind(cos(theta), sin(theta))
  L      <- chol(sigma)
  ell    <- t(L) %*% circle
  data.frame(
    x_scaled = mu[1] + n_sd * ell[1, ],
    y_scaled = mu[2] + n_sd * ell[2, ]
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      rain_frac = x_scaled * rain_frac_sd + rain_frac_mean,
      swe_log   = y_scaled * swe_log_sd   + swe_log_mean,
      swe_mm    = 10^swe_log - SWE_LOG_OFFSET
    )
}

ellipses_df <- map_dfr(seq_len(fit$G), function(g) {
  mu    <- fit$parameters$mean[, g]
  sigma <- fit$parameters$variance$sigma[, , g]
  make_ellipse(mu, sigma) %>% mutate(component = factor(g))
})

p_ellipse_base <- ggplot(gmm_data,
                         aes(x = rain_frac, y = swe_mean_mm + SWE_LOG_OFFSET)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 0.7, color = "steelblue4") +
  geom_path(data = ellipses_df,
            aes(x = rain_frac, y = swe_mm + SWE_LOG_OFFSET,
                group = component, color = component),
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Component") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "l") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = SNOW_EM_THRESH, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = RAIN_EM_THRESH, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.45) +
  annotate("text", x = SNOW_EM_THRESH, y = Inf, label = "0.10",
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3, size = 2.8, color = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = RAIN_EM_THRESH, y = Inf, label = "0.95",
           hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3, size = 2.8, color = "grey30") +
  labs(
    title    = "GMM component ellipses (2 SD) — rain fraction x SWE",
    subtitle = sprintf("G = %d (%s); uncolored points", fit$G, fit$modelName),
    x        = "Rain fraction",
    y        = "Mean antecedent SWE + 1 (mm, log scale)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave(file.path(diag_dir, "gmm_ellipses_uncolored.png"),
       plot = p_ellipse_base, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 150)

# --- Validation: color by flood_type_raw -------------------------------------
p_ellipse_typed <- ggplot(gmm_data,
                           aes(x = rain_frac, y = swe_mean_mm + SWE_LOG_OFFSET,
                               color = flood_type_raw)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8) +
  geom_path(data = ellipses_df,
            aes(x = rain_frac, y = swe_mm + SWE_LOG_OFFSET,

# --- Classification change analysis ------------------------------------------
# Compare GMM component assignment against current flood_type_raw.

gmm_data <- gmm_data %>%
```

```{r rainfall-fraction-thresholds-2}
# =============================================================================
# GMM Diagnostic: Rainfall component split investigation
# Are GMM components 1 and 3 (low-SWE, high rain-fraction) physically
# distinct or a geometric artifact of data compression in that corner?
# =============================================================================

# Assign each peak to its maximum-posterior component
gmm_data <- gmm_data %>%
  mutate(
    gmm_component     = fit$classification,
    gmm_post_max      = apply(fit$z, 1, max)
  )

# Identify the two low-SWE, high rain-fraction components by finding the
# two components with the highest median rain_frac from comp_summary
top2_rain_comps <- comp_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(rain_frac_med)) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  pull(gmm_component) %>%
  sort()  # sort so labeling is consistent (lower index = comp A)

cat(sprintf("\nInvestigating rainfall split: GMM components %d and %d\n",
            top2_rain_comps[1], top2_rain_comps[2]))

rain_split <- gmm_data %>%
  filter(gmm_component %in% top2_rain_comps) %>%

    comp_label = factor(
      gmm_component,
```

```{r rainfall-fraction-thresholds-3}
# =============================================================================
# GMM Post-processing: Merge components 1+3 into unified rainfall class
# G=4 EEV solution retained as fitted; merger is a post-hoc label assignment
# based on diagnostic confirmation that components 1 and 3 are not physically
# distinct (overlapping DOY, near-identical flood magnitude distributions).
#
# Physically meaningful 3-class mapping:
#   Rainfall : GMM components 1 + 3 (merged)
#   ROS      : GMM component 2
#   Snowmelt : GMM component 4
# =============================================================================

# --- Define merged component mapping ----------------------------------------
# Identify component indices by median rain_frac from comp_summary
# (do not hardcode — derive from data in case ordering shifts)
comp_by_rain <- comp_summary %>% arrange(rain_frac_med)

# Expected order ascending rain_frac: snowmelt, ROS, rainfall_low, rainfall_high
# Component with lowest rain_frac median = snowmelt
# Component with second-lowest         = ROS
# Components with two highest          = rainfall (to be merged)
comp_snowmelt  <- comp_by_rain$gmm_component[1]
comp_ros       <- comp_by_rain$gmm_component[2]
comp_rain_low  <- comp_by_rain$gmm_component[3]
comp_rain_high <- comp_by_rain$gmm_component[4]

cat(sprintf(
  "Component mapping (by ascending median rain_frac):\n  Snowmelt : %d (median rf = %.3f)\n  ROS      : %d (median rf = %.3f)\n  Rain low : %d (median rf = %.3f)\n  Rain high: %d (median rf = %.3f)\n",
  comp_snowmelt,  comp_by_rain$rain_frac_med[1],
  comp_ros,       comp_by_rain$rain_frac_med[2],
  comp_rain_low,  comp_by_rain$rain_frac_med[3],
  comp_rain_high, comp_by_rain$rain_frac_med[4]
))

# Assign merged 3-class label
gmm_data <- gmm_data %>%
  mutate(
    gmm_class = case_when(
      gmm_component %in% c(comp_rain_low, comp_rain_high) ~ "rainfall",
      gmm_component == comp_ros                           ~ "ROS",
      gmm_component == comp_snowmelt                     ~ "snowmelt"
    ),
    gmm_class = factor(gmm_class, levels = c("rainfall", "ROS", "snowmelt"))
  )

class_summary <- gmm_data %>%
  dplyr::count(gmm_class) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)
cat("\nMerged 3-class GMM assignment:\n")
print(class_summary)

# --- Merged posterior: combine components 1+3 --------------------------------
# For boundary extraction we need merged posteriors:
#   P(rainfall) = P(comp_rain_low) + P(comp_rain_high)
#   P(ROS)      = P(comp_ros)
#   P(snowmelt) = P(comp_snowmelt)
z <- fit$z  # n x 4 posterior matrix

gmm_data <- gmm_data %>%
  mutate(
    post_rainfall = z[, comp_rain_low] + z[, comp_rain_high],
    post_ros      = z[, comp_ros],
    post_snowmelt = z[, comp_snowmelt]
  )

# --- Boundary extraction (merged posteriors) ---------------------------------
# Snowmelt/ROS boundary: P(snowmelt) = P(ROS), evaluated at median SWE of
#   snowmelt-classified events (flood_type_raw == "snowmelt")
# ROS/rainfall boundary: P(ROS) = P(rainfall), evaluated at median SWE of
#   rainfall-classified events (flood_type_raw == "rainfall")

swe_snowmelt_med <- median(
  gmm_data$swe_mean_mm[gmm_data$flood_type_raw == "snowmelt"], na.rm = TRUE)
swe_rainfall_med <- median(
  gmm_data$swe_mean_mm[gmm_data$flood_type_raw == "rainfall"], na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf(
  "\nBoundary evaluation points:\n  Snowmelt/ROS  at SWE = %.2f mm (median snowmelt SWE)\n  ROS/Rainfall  at SWE = %.2f mm (median rainfall SWE)\n",
  swe_snowmelt_med, swe_rainfall_med
))

# Function: evaluate merged posteriors across rain_frac grid at fixed SWE,
# return equal-posterior crossing between two named classes
find_merged_boundary <- function(fit, swe_mm_fixed,
                                 comp_a_idx, comp_b_idx,
                                 rain_frac_mean, rain_frac_sd,
                                 swe_log_mean,   swe_log_sd,
                                 swe_log_offset  = 1.0,
                                 n_grid          = 5000) {
  rf_grid    <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_grid)
  swe_log_f  <- log10(swe_mm_fixed + swe_log_offset)
  rf_scaled  <- (rf_grid - rain_frac_mean) / rain_frac_sd
  swe_scaled <- rep((swe_log_f - swe_log_mean) / swe_log_sd, n_grid)

  grid_mat <- cbind(rf_scaled, swe_scaled)
  z_grid   <- predict(fit, newdata = grid_mat)$z

  # comp_a_idx / comp_b_idx may be vectors (merged classes)
  post_a <- rowSums(z_grid[, comp_a_idx, drop = FALSE])
  post_b <- rowSums(z_grid[, comp_b_idx, drop = FALSE])

  diff_ab <- post_a - post_b
  crossings <- which(diff(sign(diff_ab)) != 0)

  if (length(crossings) == 0) {
    warning("No equal-posterior crossing found in [0, 1] rain_frac range")
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  # Take first crossing; interpolate
  idx <- crossings[1]
  rf_grid[idx] +
    (rf_grid[idx + 1] - rf_grid[idx]) *
    abs(diff_ab[idx]) / (abs(diff_ab[idx]) + abs(diff_ab[idx + 1]))
}

boundary_snow_ros <- find_merged_boundary(
  fit, swe_snowmelt_med,
  comp_a_idx = comp_snowmelt,
  comp_b_idx = comp_ros,
  rain_frac_mean, rain_frac_sd,
  swe_log_mean,   swe_log_sd
)

boundary_ros_rain <- find_merged_boundary(
  fit, swe_rainfall_med,
  comp_a_idx = comp_ros,
  comp_b_idx = c(comp_rain_low, comp_rain_high),
  rain_frac_mean, rain_frac_sd,
  swe_log_mean,   swe_log_sd
)

cat(sprintf(
  "\nGMM-derived rain_frac boundaries (merged 3-class):\n  Snowmelt/ROS  : %.3f  (current SNOW_EM_THRESH = %.2f)\n  ROS/Rainfall  : %.3f  (current RAIN_EM_THRESH = %.2f)\n",
  boundary_snow_ros, SNOW_EM_THRESH,
  boundary_ros_rain, RAIN_EM_THRESH
))

# --- Ellipses for all 4 GMM components (for overlay) ------------------------
ellipses_all <- map_dfr(seq_len(fit$G), function(g) {
  mu    <- fit$parameters$mean[, g]
  sigma <- fit$parameters$variance$sigma[, , g]
  make_ellipse(mu, sigma) %>%
    mutate(
      gmm_component = g,
      gmm_class     = case_when(
        g %in% c(comp_rain_low, comp_rain_high) ~ "rainfall",
        g == comp_ros                           ~ "ROS",
        g == comp_snowmelt                      ~ "snowmelt"
      )
    )
})

# --- Color schemes -----------------------------------------------------------
class_colors <- c(
  "rainfall" = "#E07B39",
  "ROS"      = "#6A9E6F",
  "snowmelt" = "#5B8DB8"
)

type_colors_full <- c(
  "rainfall"     = "#E07B39",
  "ROS"          = "#6A9E6F",
  "snowmelt"     = "#5B8DB8",
  "unclassified" = "grey70"
)

# --- Shared plot elements ----------------------------------------------------
boundary_lines <- list(
  geom_vline(xintercept = boundary_snow_ros, linetype = "solid",
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
  geom_vline(xintercept = boundary_ros_rain, linetype = "solid",
             color = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
  annotate("text", x = boundary_snow_ros, y = Inf,
           label = sprintf("GMM\n%.3f", boundary_snow_ros),
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.2, size = 2.6, color = "black"),
  annotate("text", x = boundary_ros_rain, y = Inf,
           label = sprintf("GMM\n%.3f", boundary_ros_rain),
           hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2, size = 2.6, color = "black"),
  geom_vline(xintercept = SNOW_EM_THRESH, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.45),
  geom_vline(xintercept = RAIN_EM_THRESH, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.45),
  annotate("text", x = SNOW_EM_THRESH, y = -Inf,
           label = sprintf("Cur.\n%.2f", SNOW_EM_THRESH),
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.2, size = 2.4, color = "grey40"),
  annotate("text", x = RAIN_EM_THRESH, y = -Inf,
           label = sprintf("Cur.\n%.2f", RAIN_EM_THRESH),
           hjust = -0.1, vjust = -0.2, size = 2.4, color = "grey40")
)

shared_scales <- list(
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), limits = c(0, 1)),
  scale_y_log10(),
  annotation_logticks(sides = "l")
)

shared_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ellipse_overlay <- geom_path(
  data        = ellipses_all,
  aes(x       = rain_frac,
      y       = swe_mm + SWE_LOG_OFFSET,
      group   = gmm_component),
  color       = "black",
  linewidth   = 0.55,
  linetype    = "solid",
  inherit.aes = FALSE
)

# --- Panel A: GMM merged 3-class assignment ----------------------------------
pA <- ggplot(gmm_data,
             aes(x = rain_frac,
                 y = swe_mean_mm + SWE_LOG_OFFSET,
                 color = gmm_class)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.7) +
  ellipse_overlay +
  boundary_lines +
  scale_color_manual(values = class_colors, name = "GMM class\n(merged)") +
  shared_scales +
  labs(
    title = "A — GMM merged 3-class assignment",
    x     = "Rain fraction",
    y     = "Mean antecedent SWE + 1 (mm)"
  ) +
  shared_theme

# --- Panel B: Current adaptive classification --------------------------------
pB <- ggplot(gmm_data,
             aes(x = rain_frac,
                 y = swe_mean_mm + SWE_LOG_OFFSET,
                 color = flood_type_raw)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.7) +
  ellipse_overlay +
  boundary_lines +
  scale_color_manual(values = type_colors_full, name = "Flood type\n(current)") +
  shared_scales +
  labs(
    title = "B — Current adaptive classification (flood_type_raw)",
    x     = "Rain fraction",
    y     = "Mean antecedent SWE + 1 (mm)"
  ) +
  shared_theme

# --- Combine and save --------------------------------------------------------
fig_final <- pA + pB +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "GMM 3-class boundaries vs. current adaptive classification",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "G=4 EEV, components %d+%d merged as rainfall | Snowmelt/ROS boundary: %.3f | ROS/Rainfall boundary: %.3f",
      comp_rain_low, comp_rain_high, boundary_snow_ros, boundary_ros_rain
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "grey40")
    )
  )

ggsave(
  file.path(diag_dir, "gmm_merged_3class_summary.png"),
  plot = fig_final, width = 13, height = 5.5, dpi = 150
)

fig_final
```
